elements.title: FIGURE 2 — NASA’s UNICORN
elements.content:
A large blue-outlined oval contains the NASA UNICORN framework. At the top inside the oval is the label “Enterprise Risk Management.”

Top council nodes and color coding:
- Red oval: “EC”
- Blue oval: “APMC”
- White oval with gray outline: “ASC”
- Green oval: “MSC”

Council relationships and arrows:
- APMC and EC are connected by two black diagonal arrows. The arrow from APMC toward EC is labeled “Programmatic Assessments and Recommendations.” The arrow from EC toward APMC is labeled “Program Strategic Guidance & Budget.”
- APMC and EC are also associated with the blue diagonal label “Program & Mission Decisions.”
- EC and ASC are connected by two vertical black arrows. The upward relationship is labeled “Extended EC.” The downward relationship is labeled “ASC Advice and Recommendations.”
- EC and MSC are connected by two black diagonal arrows. The relationship is labeled “Institutional Strategic Guidance & Budget.”
- EC and MSC are also associated with the green diagonal label “Mission-Enabling Decisions.”
- APMC and ASC are connected by a blue arrow labeled “APMC Participation.”
- ASC and MSC are connected by a blue, two-way relationship labeled “Extended MSC.”
- ASC and MSC are connected by a black horizontal, two-way relationship labeled “Program-derived Institutional Requirements.”
- APMC and MSC are connected by a black horizontal, two-way relationship labeled “Delivery of Institutional Capabilities.”

Risk categories, shown as adjacent colored blocks across the lower middle of the oval:
- Blue: “Political and Reputational Risk”
- Light blue: “Programmatic Risk”
- Olive green: “Financial Risk”
- Yellow: “Strategic Risk”
- Red: “Operational Risk”

The risk-category blocks sit beneath a green triangular/roof-shaped form rising to the center beneath the ASC node. Large curved green arrows on the left and right surround the framework and point around the oval.

Lower organizational layers:
- A large light-blue rounded rectangle reads: “HQ Mission Directorate Centers” and “Functional Organizations Supporting Center Operations.”
- A green rounded rectangle below it reads: “Control Certifications-Analysis of Controls” and “Fraud Risk Management.”

Color legend at the bottom:
- Red: “EC Executive Council”
- Blue: “APMC Agency Program Management Council”
- White/gray outline: “ASC Acquisition Strategy Council”
- Green: “MSC Mission Support Council”

Enterprise Risk Management
CONTINUED ON THE NEXT PAGE →
OMB Circular A-123, Management’s Responsibility for Enterprise Risk Management and Internal Control, requires 
Federal agencies to implement ERM to ensure Federal managers are effectively managing risks that could affect the 
achievement of Agency strategic objectives.
Risk management is embedded in NASA’s culture, and the principles and practices are inherent in everyday operations. 
In July 2023, the NASA Deputy Administrator directed the formation of an internal Agency Risk Management Tiger 
Team to review, assess and propose options to strengthen the Agency’s risk management framework. Specifically, 
the Tiger Team focused on identifying how to best support risk practitioners and senior leaders in managing and 
communicating their risks effectively. Based on the Tiger Team’s findings, NASA implemented several initiatives to 
improve internal risk management processes. This includes establishment of an Agency Risk Management Officer 
(ARMO) within the Headquarters Office of Safety and Mission Assurance to fortify NASA’s risk management policies, 
practices, and capabilities.
NASA’s ARMO leads the Agency’s ERM effort in collaboration with the Quality Assurance Division within OCFO. The 
NASA Unified Comprehensive Operational Risk Network (UNICORN), NASA’s ERM framework, is the framework 
for the communication and exchange of risk information between NASA’s functional organizations and the Agency 
leadership (see Figure 2). The framework is the foundation of the Agency’s risk management policy, activities, and 
decisional councils.
